title: Consumption Telemetry Enrichment and Cost Attribution PRD
author: Amelia Chen
body:
Overview:

Purpose
This PRD defines the scope, requirements, and rollout plan for the Consumption Telemetry Enrichment and Cost Attribution initiative (CTECA). The goal is to provide accurate, queryable, and auditable telemetry that maps inference consumption (tokens, embeddings, model variants, and runtime features) to cost drivers and customer-visible billing line-items. The product will enable SRE, Billing, Product, and Sales teams to reason about unit economics, run experiments, and support commercial conversations with precise, explainable usage data.

Context and motivation
- Current telemetry captures request headers, trace IDs, and coarse token counts per request. It lacks consistent enrichment for batching characteristics, KV cache hits, quantization path, and fallback routing.
- Finance and Sales frequently request post-hoc attribution for odd invoices; engineering lacks a robust signal to reconstruct per-request cost decisions.
- Observability and Optimize need richer signals to make automated recommendations and validate cost-saving experiments.

Goals (measurable)
1) Increase per-request cost attribution fidelity to >=95% of billed tokens by 2027-Q1 (measured against billing ledger sampling).
2) Provide a queryable schema and dashboard for per-tenant and per-route unit economics with 48-hour data latency SLA after rollout.
3) Emit enriched telemetry for 100% of production-hosted and dedicated requests by default (opt-out for privacy-sensitive tenants).
4) Expose a public (internal) API for reconciliations used by Finance and Support with <=30s read latency for 30-day window.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not change billing logic or pricing tiers. Mapping to invoices is advisory until Finance approves mapping rules.
- Does not include historical backfill beyond 90 days for enriched fields; retrospective sampling will be considered in a later phase.

User personas and user stories
- Finance analyst: "I need to explain a customer invoice variance by inspecting per-route tokenization and fallback events for a week of traffic."
- Support engineer: "When a customer disputes an overage, I can produce a signed reconciliation for the time range with the attribution fields."
- Product manager: "I can evaluate the effect of caching and quantization experiments on per-token cost across a tenant cohort."
- SRE: "I can set alerting tied to unexpected increases in cost-per-token for a model variant or region."

Scope and deliverables
Phase 1 (MVP) - 10 weeks
- Telemetry schema v1 with required fields (see table below).
- Server-side enrichment at the ingestion layer (gateway/service edge and dedicated proxy) to add missing fields.
- Streaming pipeline (telemetry-ingestor -> enrichment-service -> billing-mapper) for near-real-time dashboards.
- Data warehouse mapping and sample reconciliation job (daily).
- Internal dashboard (Grafana) and a simple reconciliation API endpoint for Finance.

Phase 2 - 12 weeks
- Support for dedicated and private deployments with optional PII redaction policies.
- SDK/agent for on-prem customers to surface local routing decisions into telemetry.
- Historical sampling backfill (90 days).
- Per-tenant opt-out flags and consent audit logs.

Phase 3 - 8 weeks
- High-cardinality cost modeling (experiment cohorts), SLA for read API (<=30s), and multi-tenant aggregation controls.
- Integration with Optimize conductor for automated recommendations.

Functional requirements
- FR-1: Every inference request must include a canonical request_id and trace_id and be associated with tenant_id and route_id.
- FR-2: Enrichment-service must add the following fields when available: model_variant, sequence_length, input_token_count, output_token_count, batching_type (single/continuous/batch), batch_size_at_inference, kv_cache_hit_rate, quantization_path (fp16/int8/q4), kernel_profile_id, fallback_reason (if fallback occurred), probe_latency_ms, and routing_tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
- FR-3: Telemetry must include feature flags active for that request (e.g., streaming=true, function_calling=true) to enable feature-level cost breakdowns.
- FR-4: All events must be signed with the cluster key and stored with an integrity checksum for reconciliation audits.
- FR-5: Enriched events must be forwarded to the telemetry-ingestor topic with <=250ms added latency at p95.

Non-functional requirements
- NFR-1: Data retention for enriched telemetry: 90 days in hot store, 2 years in cold archive.
- NFR-2: 99.9% uptime for enrichment-service and ingestion pipeline.
- NFR-3: Observability: 1m resolution metrics for enrichment success rate and enrichment latency.
- NFR-4: Privacy: For tenants flagged "restricted", the telemetry must redact prompt text and any user identifiers before enrichment.
- NFR-5: Cost: The telemetry pipeline should add no more than 5% overhead to total inference cost for the first 6 months of operation.

Telemetry schema (human-readable table)
- request_id: string (canonical unique id assigned at gateway)
- trace_id: string (distributed trace)
- tenant_id: string
- route_id: string
- timestamp_iso: string
- model_variant: string (e.g., redwood-v1.3-q4)
- input_token_count: integer
- output_token_count: integer
- sequence_length: integer
- batching_type: string (single|continuous|batch)
- batch_size_at_inference: integer
- kv_cache_hit_rate: float (0.0-1.0)
- quantization_path: string (fp16|int8|q4)
- kernel_profile_id: string
- fallback_reason: string|null
- routing_tier: string (hosted|dedicated|private)
- feature_flags: list[string] (e.g., ["streaming","function_calling"])
- cost_units_estimate: float (internal cents-equivalent per-request)
- signed_checksum: string

API surface and query patterns
- /internal/reconcile?tenant_id=&start=&end=&route_id= (returns aggregated attribution, sample payloads, and signed reconciliation artifact)
- /internal/costs/route?route_id=&window_days= (time-series of cost-per-token, kv-cache impact)
- SQL-ready warehouse tables: enriched_events_vw, daily_reconcile_summary, cost_model_events

Data and billing mapping logic (high-level)
1) Per-request token counts converted to billable units using the active pricing map for the model_variant and routing_tier.
2) Apply caching discounts: if kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.5, attribute only miss tokens to billable units.
3) Quantization path multiplier applied to CPU/GPU kernel costs (tunable: fp16->1.0, q4->0.6, int8->0.55).
4) Batch amortization: per-request cost = compute_cost / batch_size_at_inference + fixed-network-cost.
Note: Final billing remains authoritative; this logic is for attribution and reconciliation only. Changes require Finance sign-off.

Rollout and migration plan
- Week 0: Integration plan and schema v1 finalized; communicate to stakeholders.
- Week 1-2: Implement enrichment at gateway (hosted) and verify end-to-end delivery to staging telemetry-ingestor.
- Week 3: Deploy MVP to 10% of production traffic (low-risk tenants) with sampling and reconciliation job enabled.
- Week 4-5: Validate reconciliation against billing for sampled tenants; tune cost conversion multipliers.
- Week 6: Expand to 50% traffic; onboard dashboard consumers (Finance, Support).
- Week 8-10: 100% rollout for hosted tenants; begin dedicated deployment enablement in Phase 2.
- Backout plan: revert enrichment toggle at gateway and disable forwarding to enrichment-service. Reconciliation remains disabled while investigation occurs.

Privacy, security and compliance considerations
- Sensitive data (prompts, PII) must be redacted prior to enrichment for tenants with restricted confidentiality or for private deployments. This is enforced by the edge proxy using tenant metadata.
- Signed checksums and signed reconciliation artifacts must be stored in an immutable ledger (S3 with Object Lock / Vault) for a configurable retention period.
- Access to reconciliation API restricted to Finance and Support roles via RBAC. Audit logs recorded for every export.

Observability and SLOs
- Enrichment success rate >= 99% (per day) after rollout.
- Enrichment added latency at p95 <= 250ms.
- Reconciliation API p95 read latency <= 30s for queries covering 30 days.
- Alerting: enrichment_success_rate < 98% for 10 minutes triggers P1 runbook.

Testing and validation
- Unit tests for enrichment rules and cost mapping logic with coverage for edge cases (fallbacks, partial KV hits).
- E2E tests: simulate traffic patterns (high-batch vs conversational) and verify cost attribution against a ground-truth simulator.
- Reconciliation smoke runs comparing daily summaries to billing ledger for sampled tenants for 14 consecutive days before full rollout.

Ownership and stakeholders
- Product owner: Amelia Chen (product)
- Engineering lead: Diego Morales (serving-runtime)
- Data engineering: Priya Nair
- Finance lead: Evan Brooks
- SRE partner: Katerina Volkova

Open decisions (to be resolved in design review)
- D1: Final multipliers for quantization and kernel_profile mapping — proposed defaults included above, Finance must approve.
- D2: Default retention policy for reconciliation artifacts — 1 year vs 2 years.
- D3: Whether to include deterministic prompt fingerprints (hashes) in telemetry for quality debugging while remaining privacy-compliant.

Appendix
- CLI example to request reconciliation artifact (internal only):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal-api.redwood.local/internal/reconcile?tenant_id=acme&start=2026-10-01&end=2026-10-07" -o acme-reconcile-20261007.json

- Example enriched event (JSON truncated, stored in warehouse view):
  {
    "request_id": "r_1234abcd",
    "tenant_id": "acme",
    "model_variant": "redwood-v2-q4",
    "input_token_count": 42,
    "output_token_count": 126,
    "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.67,
    "quantization_path": "q4",
    "batching_type": "continuous",
    "batch_size_at_inference": 8,
    "cost_units_estimate": 0.0034
  }

- Success metrics and dashboards: link to (internal) Grafana folder: /dashboards/telemetry/cost-attribution

Next steps
- Approve PRD and schedule design review with data engineering and finance in the next 2 weeks.
- Prepare staging integration checklist and sampling tenants list.
